This message comes from Capital One with the Venture X card.
Earn unlimited double miles and a $300 annual Capital One travel credit.
Capital One.
What's in your wallet?
Terms of fly.
Details at CapitalOne.com.
Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Corva Coleman.
President Trump has vowed to campaign for Republican candidates in 35 of the country's
most competitive races, but he's kicking off his campaign stops today in Oklahoma.
Democrats a solidly Republican state, not considered a battleground.
And Piers Franco-Artones says Trump will be able to test some of his campaign pitches
on GOP voters.
This is partly making sure that his supporters show up, Trump's supporters.
The challenge that Republicans have long had is turning out low propensity voters when Trump
is not on the ballot.
And this trip to Oklahoma and Alabama is part of an effort to make sure those voters do
come out next month for the midterms.
And Piers Franco-Artones reporting.
A group of small companies and nearly two dozen states are challenging President Trump's
latest effort to impose double-digit tariffs on nearly everything the U.S. imports.
NPR's Scott Horsley reports opponents of the tariffs have made their case before a specialized
trade court.
After two earlier rounds of worldwide tariffs were struck down by the courts, the Trump
administration imposed a new set of import taxes, relying on a different trade law called
Section 301.
Plaintiffs lawyer Pratik Shah argues that law is designed to go after individual countries
that behave badly, not virtually every U.S. trading partner.
"It would be a massive transfer of taxing power from Congress to the executive to allow
them to forego the country-specific sort of findings that 301 requires."
U.S. importers paid more than $20 billion in tariffs last month, but the government
also refunded $11 billion from earlier tariffs that were ruled illegal.
Scott Horsley in Fair News, Washington.
The Senate has confirmed Acting Labor Secretary Keith Sonderling to the position.
Sonderling has run the agency since former Labor Secretary Lori Chavez-Darimer left.
She had been accused of abusing her office.
Britain's prime minister says U.K. authorities have strong indications Iran was involved
in an incident last weekend near an airbase in England that U.S. forces also use.
Five men were arrested.
Philip Marks reports from London British and U.S. officials are jointly investigating.
Police detained the British men all in their 20s and from London on Sunday near RAF Fairford,
a base American bombers have flown from during this year's strikes on Iran.
They were held on suspicion of explosives offenses and preparing an act of terrorism,
then released on bail the next day.
Police say three small trucks found at the scene contained gasoline but no explosives.
Speaking to British broadcasters, Prime Minister Andy Burnham offered little concrete information
about the alleged plot or Iran's potential involvement, adding only the investigation
remains complex and serious and he'd share more details soon.
Iran denies any role, though has previously warned that any bases used to attack its territory
would constitute legitimate targets.
For NPR News, I'm Willem Marks in London.
This is NPR.
Tennessee failed to kill a condemned inmate last night.
Christa Pike was given a lethal injection two times.
She survived and was moved to a hospital.
Pike's attorneys say she was clearly alive and snoring after Tennessee's second botched
execution this year.
Tennessee Governor Bill Lee has halted the state's remaining execution scheduled for
this year.
President Trump has announced that South Korea will invest $200 billion in energy projects
in the U.S.
It's part of a $350 billion investment deal that South Korea agreed to last year.
NPR's Anthony Kuhn reports from Seoul this is in exchange for lower U.S. tariffs.
The projects include a gas-fired power plant in Texas, eight large nuclear power plants
in several states, and investment in a natural gas pipeline in Alaska.
President Trump called the projects a major step toward securing the U.S.'s energy supply
chain.
This announcement's timing is widely seen as a bid to burnish Trump's economic record
ahead of midterm elections.
South Korea's Ministry of Industry, though, says in a statement that there's been no
decision on whether or how much South Korea will invest in the Alaska pipeline.
A U.S. Commerce Department fact sheet says that whether work on the project goes ahead
depends on whether it's considered commercially viable.
Anthony Kuhn in PR News, Seoul.
Both officials in Pennsylvania have confirmed a fifth measles-associated death in the state.
The affected person was not vaccinated.
There have been well over 900 confirmed measles cases in Pennsylvania during this outbreak.
It's NPR.
